story.en: Freshworks' Sales Ops team, ahead of a board review, needs a report of "business leads by company email domain" — but the leads table doubles as a catch-all for every inbound channel: cold calls where only a phone number was captured (email genuinely NULL, not yet collected), and a trade-show badge-scanner that occasionally mangles an email during OCR, dropping the '@' entirely and leaving something that looks like a domain but isn't a real email at all. Personal-provider addresses (gmail.com, yahoo.com, etc.) don't count as a "company" for this report either — leadership only wants to see actual business domains that sales could plausibly qualify.
story.ta: Freshworks-oda Sales Ops team-la, board review varradhukku munnadi, 'company email domain vaari business leads' report venum — aana leads table ella inbound channel-kkum catch-all-a irukku: cold call-la phone number mattum kudutha (email genuine-a innum edhuvum kudukkala, ippozhudhu-varaikkum collect pannala), matrum trade-show badge-scanner sila neram OCR-la email-a mangle pannitu, '@'-a completely drop pannitu, domain madhiri theriyura aana real email illaadha edho onnu vachiruvaan. Personal-provider addresses (gmail.com, yahoo.com, etc.) indha report-kku 'company' nu count aagaadhu-nu-um — leadership, sales qualify panna mudiyura real business domains mattum-thaan paakka virumburanga.
story.hi: Freshworks ki Sales Ops team ko, board review se pehle, 'company email domain ke hisaab se business leads' ki report chahiye — lekin leads table har inbound channel ke liye ek catch-all hai: cold calls jahan sirf phone number liya gaya (email genuinely abhi tak nahi diya gaya, abhi tak collect nahi hua), aur ek trade-show badge-scanner jo kabhi-kabhi OCR mein email ko mangle kar deta hai, '@' ko poori tarah drop kar deta hai, aur kuch aisa chhod deta hai jo domain jaisa dikhta hai lekin asal email hai hi nahi. Personal-provider addresses (gmail.com, yahoo.com, waghera) bhi is report ke liye 'company' nahi maane jaate — leadership sirf un asal business domains ko dekhna chahti hai jinhe sales qualify kar sake.
story.te: Freshworks Sales Ops team ki, board review mundu, 'company email domain prakaram business leads' report kavali — kani leads table prathi inbound channel ki catch-all ga untundi: cold calls lo phone number matrame icharu (email genuine ga inka evaru ivvaledu, ippativaraku collect avvaledu), mariyu oka trade-show badge-scanner konni sarlu OCR lo email ni mangle chestundi, '@' ni pooriga drop chestundi, domain la kanipinche kani real email kaani dani vidichi pedatundi. Personal-provider addresses (gmail.com, yahoo.com, ithara) kuda ee report ki 'company' ga count avvavu — leadership sales qualify cheyagalige real business domains ni matrame chudalani anukuntunnaru.

question.en: For leads that have a valid, well-formed email address (one that actually contains '@'), extract the domain — everything after the '@' — using SUBSTR and INSTR. Exclude leads with no email at all, exclude leads whose email has no '@' at all (INSTR returns 0 for those, and SUBSTR would otherwise silently treat the malformed string as its own domain), and exclude personal email providers ('gmail.com', 'yahoo.com', 'hotmail.com', 'outlook.com'). Return domain and lead_count — the number of leads at that domain — grouped by domain, ordered alphabetically by domain.
question.ta: Valid-a, well-formed email address irukkura leads-kku (adhula '@' actual-a irukkanum), SUBSTR matrum INSTR use panni domain-a — '@'-kku apparam irukkura ella-vum — extract pannunga. Edhavadhu email-e illaadha leads-a exclude pannunga, '@' edhuvum illaadha email irukkura leads-a-yum exclude pannunga (avangaluku INSTR 0 return pannum, illaana SUBSTR andha malformed string-a adhoda own domain-a silent-a treat pannidum), matrum personal email providers-a ('gmail.com', 'yahoo.com', 'hotmail.com', 'outlook.com') exclude pannunga. domain matrum lead_count-a return pannunga — andha domain-la irukkura leads-oda count — domain vaari group panni, domain alphabetical order-la order pannunga.
question.hi: Jin leads ke paas valid, well-formed email address hai (jismein asal mein '@' ho), unke liye SUBSTR aur INSTR use karke domain — '@' ke baad ka sab kuch — extract karo. Aise leads ko exclude karo jinke paas koi email hi nahi hai, aise leads ko bhi exclude karo jinke email mein '@' hi nahi hai (unke liye INSTR 0 return karta hai, warna SUBSTR us malformed string ko chup-chaap apna hi domain maan lega), aur personal email providers ('gmail.com', 'yahoo.com', 'hotmail.com', 'outlook.com') ko exclude karo. domain aur lead_count return karo — us domain par jitne leads hain unki ginti — domain ke hisaab se group karke, domain ke alphabetical order mein sort karo.
question.te: Valid, well-formed email address unna leads ki (danilo actual ga '@' undali), SUBSTR mariyu INSTR upayoginchi domain ni — '@' tarvata unna anni — extract cheyandi. E email e leni leads ni exclude cheyandi, '@' e lenna email unna leads ni kuda exclude cheyandi (vaalliki INSTR 0 return chestundi, ledante SUBSTR aa malformed string ni dani own domain ga silent ga treat chestundi), mariyu personal email providers ('gmail.com', 'yahoo.com', 'hotmail.com', 'outlook.com') ni exclude cheyandi. domain mariyu lead_count ni return cheyandi — aa domain lo unna leads count — domain prakaram group chesi, domain alphabetical order lo sort cheyandi.

title.en: Look at every lead's email and where '@' sits in it
title.ta: Ovvoru lead-oda email-a-yum, adhula '@' engaya irukkunu-yum paakkunga
title.hi: Har lead ke email ko aur usmein '@' kahan hai use dekho
title.te: Prathi lead email ni mariyu danilo '@' ekkada undo chudandi

en: INSTR(email, '@') returns the 1-based position of '@' inside the string — Priya's email has '@' at position 13, Divya's at position 6, and so on; this is the building block the rest of the query relies on.
Karthik Iyer (lead_id 4) has a genuinely NULL email — he came in through a cold call and only gave a phone number, so INSTR(NULL, '@') itself returns NULL, not 0 or an error.

Rohan Malhotra's (lead_id 6) email is 'rohanmalhotracorp.com' — a trade-show badge scan mangled it and dropped the '@' entirely — so INSTR returns 0, not NULL; 0 and NULL are two different signals for two different problems and need to be handled differently.
Nothing is extracted or filtered yet — this step exists purely to see, row by row, which leads have a real '@', which have none, and which have no email at all.
ta: INSTR(email, '@'), string-la '@' irukkura 1-based position-a return pannum — Priya-oda email-la '@' position 13-la irukku, Divya-oda 6-la irukku, ipdi; idhu-thaan meedhi query relying pannura building block.
Karthik Iyer-kku (lead_id 4) genuine-a NULL email irukku — avaru cold call-la varunga, phone number mattum kudutharu, so INSTR(NULL, '@') adhuve NULL return pannum, 0 alladhu error illa.

Rohan Malhotra-oda (lead_id 6) email 'rohanmalhotracorp.com' — trade-show badge scan adha mangle pannitu, '@'-a completely drop pannitu — so INSTR 0 return pannum, NULL illa; 0 matrum NULL rendu vera vera problem-kku rendu vera vera signal, avanga-a vera vera-a handle pannanum.
Innum edhuvum extract alladhu filter pannala — indha step, row row-a, evanga-kku real '@' irukku, evanga-kku illa, matrum evanga-kku email-e illa nu paakkuradhu-kku mattum-thaan.
hi: INSTR(email, '@') string ke andar '@' ki 1-based position return karta hai — Priya ke email mein '@' position 13 par hai, Divya ke mein 6 par, aise hi; yahi wo building block hai jis par baaki query depend karti hai.
Karthik Iyer (lead_id 4) ka email genuinely NULL hai — wo cold call se aaye the aur sirf phone number diya tha, isliye INSTR(NULL, '@') khud NULL return karta hai, 0 ya error nahi.

Rohan Malhotra (lead_id 6) ka email 'rohanmalhotracorp.com' hai — ek trade-show badge scan ne ise mangle kar diya aur '@' ko poori tarah drop kar diya — isliye INSTR 0 return karta hai, NULL nahi; 0 aur NULL do alag problems ke liye do alag signals hain aur inhe alag tarike se handle karna padta hai.
Abhi kuch bhi extract ya filter nahi hua — yeh step sirf yeh dekhne ke liye hai, row by row, kis lead ke paas real '@' hai, kiske paas nahi hai, aur kiske paas email hi nahi hai.
te: INSTR(email, '@') string lo '@' unna 1-based position ni return chestundi — Priya email lo '@' position 13 lo undi, Divya di 6 lo undi, ila; idi ne migatha query depend ayye building block.
Karthik Iyer ki (lead_id 4) genuine ga NULL email undi — ayana cold call dwara vacharu, phone number matrame icharu, so INSTR(NULL, '@') adi ne NULL return chestundi, 0 leda error kaadu.

Rohan Malhotra (lead_id 6) email 'rohanmalhotracorp.com' — oka trade-show badge scan dani mangle chesi, '@' ni pooriga drop chesindi — so INSTR 0 return chestundi, NULL kaadu; 0 mariyu NULL rendu vere vere problems ki rendu vere vere signals, vaatini vere vere ga handle cheyali.
Inka emi extract cheyaledu leda filter cheyaledu — ee step row row ga, evariki real '@' undo, evariki ledo, mariyu evariki email e ledo chudadaniki matrame.

title.en: The trap: filtering NULL isn't enough
title.ta: Trap: NULL mattum filter pannradhu podhaadhu
title.hi: Trap: sirf NULL filter karna kaafi nahi hai
title.te: Trap: NULL matrame filter cheyadam saripodu

steps.sql:
SELECT SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email,'@')+1) AS domain, COUNT(*) AS lead_count
FROM leads
WHERE email IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY domain
ORDER BY lead_count DESC, domain;

en: WHERE email IS NOT NULL correctly drops Karthik Iyer's row, so that part of the fix looks solid at a glance.
Rohan Malhotra's row survives the filter, because his email isn't NULL — it's just malformed — and INSTR('rohanmalhotracorp.com', '@') returns 0, not NULL.

SUBSTR(email, 0+1) is SUBSTR(email, 1), which returns the entire original string starting from its first character — so Rohan's whole mangled email becomes its own fake 'domain,' sitting in the results as if it were a real company.

gmail.com shows up with a count of 2, mixed in right alongside genuine business domains like freshdesk.io and zylker.com — this query never asked whether a domain belongs to a personal provider, so it can't tell them apart yet.
ta: WHERE email IS NOT NULL, Karthik Iyer-oda row-a correct-a drop pannum, so andha fix part first look-la solid-a theriyum.
Rohan Malhotra-oda row filter-a survive pannum, ention avaroda email NULL illa — adhu just malformed — matrum INSTR('rohanmalhotracorp.com', '@') 0 return pannum, NULL illa.

SUBSTR(email, 0+1) ippodhu SUBSTR(email, 1)-a irukkum, adhu original string-a mudhal character-la irundhu full-a return pannum — so Rohan-oda mulukka mangled email adhoda own fake 'domain'-a maarikkum, real company madhiri results-la sit pannikittu irukkum.

gmail.com count 2-oda varum, freshdesk.io matrum zylker.com madhiri genuine business domains-oda kalandhu — indha query domain personal provider-kku sondhamaa nu edhuvum kekkave illa, so idhu avatha innum vera pannave mudiyaadhu.
hi: WHERE email IS NOT NULL Karthik Iyer ki row ko sahi tarike se drop karta hai, isliye fix ka wo hissa pehli nazar mein theek lagta hai.
Rohan Malhotra ki row filter se bach jaati hai, kyunki unka email NULL nahi hai — wo bas malformed hai — aur INSTR('rohanmalhotracorp.com', '@') 0 return karta hai, NULL nahi.

SUBSTR(email, 0+1) asal mein SUBSTR(email, 1) hai, jo poori original string ko uske pehle character se return karta hai — isliye Rohan ka poora mangled email khud apna fake 'domain' ban jaata hai, results mein aise baitha rehta hai jaise wo koi asli company ho.

gmail.com count 2 ke saath dikhta hai, freshdesk.io aur zylker.com jaise genuine business domains ke sath mila hua — is query ne kabhi yeh nahi poocha ki koi domain personal provider ka hai ya nahi, isliye yeh abhi unhe alag nahi kar sakta.
te: WHERE email IS NOT NULL, Karthik Iyer row ni correct ga drop chestundi, so aa fix part first look lo solid ga kanipistundi.
Rohan Malhotra row filter nunchi survive avutundi, endukante ayana email NULL kaadu — adi just malformed — mariyu INSTR('rohanmalhotracorp.com', '@') 0 return chestundi, NULL kaadu.

SUBSTR(email, 0+1) ante SUBSTR(email, 1), adi original string ni dani modati character nunchi full ga return chestundi — so Rohan mottham mangled email dani own fake 'domain' ga maripotundi, results lo real company la kuchuni untundi.

gmail.com count 2 tho vastundi, freshdesk.io mariyu zylker.com la genuine business domains tho kalisi — ee query domain personal provider di aa ani eppudu adagaledu, so idi vaatini inka vere cheyalenu.

title.en: Fix it: guard against INSTR = 0 and drop personal domains
title.ta: Fix pannunga: INSTR = 0-kku guard vachi, personal domains-a drop pannunga
title.hi: Fix karo: INSTR = 0 se guard lagao aur personal domains ko drop karo
title.te: Fix cheyandi: INSTR = 0 ki guard pettandi, personal domains ni drop cheyandi

steps.sql:
SELECT SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email,'@')+1) AS domain, COUNT(*) AS lead_count
FROM leads
WHERE email IS NOT NULL
  AND INSTR(email,'@') > 0
  AND SUBSTR(email, INSTR(email,'@')+1) NOT IN ('gmail.com','yahoo.com','hotmail.com','outlook.com')
GROUP BY domain
ORDER BY domain;

en: AND INSTR(email,'@') > 0 is the fix step 2 was missing — it explicitly rejects Rohan Malhotra's malformed email, because a 0 means 'no @ found at all,' not 'found one at the very start.'
WHERE email IS NOT NULL and INSTR(email,'@') > 0 together cover both failure modes from step 1: a lead with no email address at all, and a lead with an email string that isn't shaped like one.
The NOT IN list removes gmail.com and yahoo.com, so Arjun, Divya, and Aditya's personal-provider leads drop out of the count entirely, leaving only domains that plausibly belong to an actual company.

Three domains survive: freshdesk.io, techflow.io, and zylker.com, each with lead_count = 1 — a small, clean result that's the direct payoff of stacking three separate filters instead of trusting any single one of them alone.
ta: AND INSTR(email,'@') > 0-thaan step 2-la missing-a irundha fix — idhu Rohan Malhotra-oda malformed email-a explicit-a reject pannum, ention 0 nu solradhu 'edhavadhu @ kandupidikave illa' nu artham, 'romba first-la kandupidichom' nu illa.

WHERE email IS NOT NULL matrum INSTR(email,'@') > 0 serndhu step 1-la irundha rendu failure modes-a-yum cover pannum: edhavadhu email-e illaadha lead, matrum email madhiri illaadha oru email string irukkura lead.

NOT IN list gmail.com matrum yahoo.com-a remove pannum, so Arjun, Divya, matrum Aditya-oda personal-provider leads count-la irundhu completely-a drop aagum, mudhula real company-kku sondhamaa irukkura domains mattum-thaan meedhi irukkum.

Moondru domains survive aaguthu: freshdesk.io, techflow.io, matrum zylker.com, ovvoruthar-kkum lead_count = 1 — moondru vera vera filters-a stack panradhula irundhu kidaikkura oru small, clean result, oru filter mattum nambradhukku pathila.
hi: AND INSTR(email,'@') > 0 hi wo fix hai jo step 2 mein missing tha — yeh Rohan Malhotra ke malformed email ko explicitly reject karta hai, kyunki 0 ka matlab hai 'bilkul koi @ nahi mila,' na ki 'bilkul shuru mein mil gaya.'

WHERE email IS NOT NULL aur INSTR(email,'@') > 0 milkar step 1 ke dono failure modes ko cover karte hain: aisa lead jiska koi email hi nahi hai, aur aisa lead jiska email string email jaisa dikhta hi nahi.

NOT IN list gmail.com aur yahoo.com ko remove karti hai, isliye Arjun, Divya, aur Aditya ke personal-provider leads count se poori tarah drop ho jaate hain, sirf wahi domains bachte hain jo asal mein kisi company ke ho sakte hain.

Teen domains bach jaate hain: freshdesk.io, techflow.io, aur zylker.com, har ek ka lead_count = 1 — ek chhota, saaf result jo teen alag-alag filters ko ek saath stack karne ka seedha fayda hai, sirf ek filter par bharosa karne ke bajaye.
te: AND INSTR(email,'@') > 0 ne step 2 lo missing ayina fix — idi Rohan Malhotra malformed email ni explicit ga reject chestundi, endukante 0 ante 'e @ e dorakaledu' ani ardham, 'chala modatlo dorikindi' ani kaadu.
WHERE email IS NOT NULL mariyu INSTR(email,'@') > 0 kalisi step 1 lo unna rendu failure modes ni cover chestayi: e email e leni lead, mariyu email la kanipinchani email string unna lead.

NOT IN list gmail.com mariyu yahoo.com ni remove chestundi, so Arjun, Divya, mariyu Aditya personal-provider leads count nunchi pooriga drop avutayi, migilindi real company di ani anipinche domains matrame.

Mudu domains survive avutayi: freshdesk.io, techflow.io, mariyu zylker.com, prathi okkati lead_count = 1 tho — mudu vere vere filters ni stack chesinanduku vachina oka small, clean result, oka filter ni matrame nammakunda.
